title: Founder Access is currently non-operational, so Founders must edit Scaffold Artifacts through ordinary Atlas Edit Proposal cycles
content:
A.2.2.1.1.3.2.1 carves out a short-term reality check against the mechanism defined immediately above it: "In the short term, 'Founder Access' will not be operational. Instead, if a Prime Founder wishes to edit their Scaffold Artifact, they must use the customary Atlas Edit Proposal processes" — the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle (A.1.11.2) or Atlas Edit Monthly Cycle (A.1.12.2).

This inverts the designed property of the pre-Transformation stage. A.2.2.1.2.4.1.1 promises the Founder "unilateral authority" with no vote or Facilitator approval required; in practice, every Scaffold edit becomes a governance item on an ecosystem-wide cycle. The intended fast, private, iterative setup phase is temporarily a slow, public, batched one.

It is worth recording as an explicit tension rather than a footnote, because it changes who bears Agent-formation cost. Under the designed path, the Founder absorbs the work of getting the Artifact right. Under the interim path, Atlas governance absorbs it — every prospective Agent's setup edits compete for the same weekly and monthly cycle attention.

The clause also demonstrates a general Atlas habit: rather than deferring publication of a mechanism until it can run, the Atlas publishes the target design and annotates the deviation. That keeps the specification stable while the implementation catches up, but means a reader must check for suspension clauses before relying on any described mechanism.
description: A documented gap between design and practice: the unilateral fast path exists on paper while real Scaffold edits queue through the weekly or monthly Atlas Edit cycle.
